title: Finite lifting tests recognize the natural Cartesian marking
statement: Use marked simplicial sets and the finite maps (i), (ii), (iii) and $A^\flat\to A$ of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], and arbitrary-base cartesian fibrations and natural markings of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. Let $S$ be any small simplicial set. Let $J_S$ consist of every map of types (i), (ii), (iii) equipped with every simplicial map from its codomain to $S$, and of $A_s^\flat\to A_s$ for each vertex $s\in S_0$, where both base maps are constant at $s$. For a small marked map $p:(X,M)\to S^\sharp$, the following conditions are equivalent: (a) every commutative square with left side in $J_S$ and right side $p$ admits a marked diagonal over $S$; (b) $X\to S$ is a cartesian fibration and $M$ is exactly its set of cartesian edges. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ or $X$ and no relative model structure is assumed.
